entries.title: The \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling problem on graphs
entries.review: Summary: An \(L(2,1)\)-labeling of a graph \(G\) is a function \(f\) from the vertex set \(V(G)\) to the set of all nonnegative integers such that \(|f(x)-f(y)|\geq2\) if \(d(x,y)=1\) and \(|f(x)-f(y)\geq 1\) if \(d(x,y)=2\). The \(L(2,1)\)-labeling number \(\lambda(G)\) of \(G\) is the smallest number \(k\) such that \(G\) has an \(L(2,1)\)-labeling with \(\max\{f(v):v\in V(G)\}=k\). We generalize the \(L(2,1)\)-labeling to the \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling in this paper. We firstly define vertex 3-coloring, 3-chromatic number \(\chi_3(G)\) and other related concepts, and give the upper bound of 3-chromatic number \(\chi_3(G)\) we then derive \(\lambda_3(G)\leq 3(\max_{H\subseteq G}\delta(H)) (\Delta^2-\Delta+1)\) for any graph \(G\) with maximum degree \(\Delta\); finally, we prove that \(\lambda_3(G)\leq 15(\Delta^2-\Delta+1)\) for any planar graph \(G\) with maximum degree \(\Delta\), and give upper bounds of \(\lambda_3(G)\) of several other graphs.

entries.title: The \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling problem for trees
entries.source: Journal of Mathematical Research with Applications
entries.review: Summary: An \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling of a graph \(G\) is a function \(f\) from the vertex set \(V(G)\) to the set of all non-negative integers(labels) such that \(|f(u) - f(v)| \ge 3\) if \(d(u,v) = 1\), \(|f(u) - f(v)| \ge 2\) if \(d(u,v) = 2\) and \(|f(u) - f(v)| \ge 1\) if \(d(u,v) = 3\). For a non-negative integer \(k\), a \(k\)-\(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling is an \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling such that no label is greater than \(k\). The \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling number of \(G\), denoted by \({\lambda_{3,2,1}}(G)\), is the smallest number \(k\) such that \(G\) has a \(k\)-\(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling. In this article, we characterize the \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling numbers of trees with diameter at most 6.

The \(L(2,1)\)-labeling number \(\lambda(G)\) of \(G\) is the smallest number \(k\) such that \(G\) has an \(L(2,1)\)-labeling with \(\max\{f(v): v\in V(G)\}= k\). entries.title: \(L(3,2,1)\) labeling of firecracker graph
entries.source: Journal of the Indonesian Mathematical Society
entries.review: Summary: Let \(G = (V, E)\) be a graph. An \(L(3,2,1)\) labeling of \(G\) is a function \(f : V \to \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}\) such that for every \(u, v \in V\), \(|f(u) - f(v)| \geq 3\) if \(d(u, v) = 1\), \(|f(u) - f(v)| \geq 2\) if \(d(u, v) = 2\), and \(|f(u) - f(v)| \geq 1\) if \(d(u, v) = 3\). Let \(k \in \mathbb{N}\), a \(k\)-\(L(3, 2, 1)\) labeling is a labeling \(L(3,2,1)\) where all labels are not greater than \(k\). An \(L(3,2,1)\) number of \(G\), denoted by \(\lambda_{3,2,1} (G)\), is the smallest non-negative integer \(k\) such that \(G\) has a \(k\)-\(L(3,2,1)\) labeling. In this paper, we determine \(\lambda_{3,2,1}\) of firecracker graphs.

entries.title: \(L(3, 2, 1)\)-labeling of the square of cycles
entries.review: It is known that the frequency assignment problem is both hard and interesting due to its potential for applications in a variety of real engineering problems. Such problems can be modeled as vertex coloring problems and hence attract graph coloring specialists to try to offer their solutions to hot problems. The authors of this paper attempt one such problem called the L(3,2,1) labeling problem and compute useful bounds for graphs such as squares of cycles. This labeling has applications in coding theory, signal processing, etc., and raised a few open problems.

entries.title: \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling for cylindrical grid: the Cartesian product of a path and a cycle
entries.review: Summary: An \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling for the graph \(G=(V,E)\) is an assignment \(f\) of a label to each vertices of \(G\) such that \(|f(u)-f(v)| \geq 4-k\) when \(\text{dist}(u,v)=k\leq3\). The \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling number, denoted by \(\lambda_{3,2,1}(G)\), for \(G\) is the smallest number \(N\) such that there is an \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling for \(G\) with span \(N\). In this paper, we compute the \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling number \(\lambda_{3,2,1}(G)\) when \(G\) is a cylindrical grid, which is the cartesian product \(P_m\square C_n\) of the path and the cycle, when \(m\geq 4\) and \(n\geq 138\). Especially when \(n\) is a multiple of \(4\), or \(m=4\) and \(n\) is a multiple of \(6\), then we have \(\lambda_{3,2,1}(G)=11\). Otherwise \(\lambda_{3,2,1}(G)=12\).

entries.title: Frequency assignment through combinatorial optimization approach
entries.review: Summary: An \(L(2,1)\)-labeling of a graph \(G\) is a function \(f\) from the vertex set \(V(G)\) to the set of all nonnegative integers such that \(|f(x)-f(y)|\geq 2\) if \(d(x,y) =1\) and \(|f(x)-f(y)|\geq 1\) if \(d(x,y)=2\). The \(L (2,1)\)-labeling number \(\lambda (G)\) of \(G\) is the smallest number \(k\) such that \(G\) has an \(L(2,1)\)-labeling with \(\max\{f(v):v\in V(G)\}=k\). We study the \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling which is a generalization of the \(L(2,1)\)-labeling on the graph formed by the (Cartesian) product and composition of 3 graphs and derive the upper bounds of \(\lambda_3(G)\) of the graph.

entries.title: The \(L (3,2,1)\)-labeling of Goldberg snark graphs
entries.source: Journal of Northeast Normal University. Natural Science Edition
entries.review: Summary: The \(L (3, 2, 1)\)-labeling problem of a Goldberg snark graph \(B_k\) is considered. The bounds for the \(L (3, 2, 1)\)-labeling number of Goldberg snark \(B_k\) are given by \(11 \leq \lambda_{3, 2, 1} (B_k) \leq 16\).

entries.title: \(L(3,2,1)\)-labelling of graphs
entries.review: Summary: For a given undirected graph \(G\), an \(L(3, 2, 1)\)-labelling is defined as a function \(f:V(G) \to \{0, 1, 2, \dots \}\) such that \(| f(u)-f(v)| \geq 3\) when \(d_G(u, v)=1\), \(| f(u)-f(v)| \geq 2\) when \(d_G(u,v) = 2\) and \(| f(u) - f(v)| \geq 1\) when \(d_G(u, v) = 1\). A \(k-L(3, 2, 1)\)-labelling is an \(L(3, 2, 1)\)-labelling such that no label is greater than \(k\). The \(L(3, 2, 1)\)-labelling number of \(G\), denoted by \(\lambda_3(G)\), is the smallest number \(k\) such that \(G\) has a \(k-L(3, 2, 1)\)-labelling. This paper gives the values of \(L(3, 2, 1)\)-labelling number for path, cycle and tree. Moreover, an upper bound of \(\lambda_3(G)\) is given for any graph.

entries.title: The \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling on bipartite graphs
entries.review: Summary: An \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling of a graph \(G\) is a function from the vertex set \(V(G)\) to the set of all nonnegative integers such that \(|f(u)-f(v)|\geq 3\) if \(d_G(u,v)=1, |f(u)-f(v)|\geq 2\) if \(d_G(u,v)=2\), and \(|f(u)-f(v)|\geq 1\) if \(d_G(u,v)=3\). The \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling problem is to find the smallest number \(\lambda_3(G)\) such that there exists an \(L(3,2,1)\)-labeling function with no label greater than it. This paper studies the problem for bipartite graphs. We obtain some bounds of \(\lambda_3\) for bipartite graphs and its subclasses. Moreover, we provide a best possible condition for a tree \(T\) such that \(\lambda_3(T)\) attains the minimum value.

entries.title: Frequency assignment model of zero divisor graph
entries.review: Summary: Given a frequency assignment network model is a zero divisor graph \(\Gamma= (V,E)\) of commutative ring \(R_\eta\), in this model, each node is considered to be a channel and their labelings are said to be the frequencies, which are assigned by the \(L(2,1)\) and \(L(3,2,1)\) labeling constraints. For a graph \(\Gamma\), \((L(2,1)\) labeling is a nonnegative real valued function \(f:V(G) \longrightarrow [0,\infty)\) such that \(\mid f(x)-f(y)\mid\geq 2d\) if \(d=1\) and \(\mid f(x)-f(y)\mid\geq d\) if \(d=2\) where \(x\) and \(y\) are any two vertices in \(V\) and \(d>0\) is a distance between \(x\) and \(y\). Similarly, one can extend this distance labeling terminology up to the diameter of a graph in order to enhance the channel clarity and to prevent the overlapping of signal produced with the minimum resource (frequency) provided. In general, this terminology is known as the \(L(h,k)\) labeling where \(h\) is the difference of any two vertex frequencies connected by a two length path. In this paper, our aim is to find the minimum spanning sharp upper frequency bound \(\lambda_{(2,1)}\) and \(\lambda_{(3,2,1)}\), within \(\Delta^2\), in terms of maximum and minimum degree of \(\Gamma\) by the distance labeling \(L(2,1)\) and \(L(3,2,1)\), respectively, for some order \(\eta= p^nq\), \(pqr\), \(p^n\) where \(p\), \(q\), \(r\) are distinct prime and \(n\) is any positive integer.
